title: 'I'm Sorry' Board
seo_title: 'I'm Sorry' Charcuterie Board for Two: How to Build It
description: An 'I'm sorry' charcuterie board: their favorite cheese, their favorite meat, their crackers and jam, plus dark chocolate and berries. How to build an apology on a board.
hook: Their favorites. All of them. This board isn't about the most impressive cheese, it's about proving you were paying attention.

items.name: Second cheese you know they like

why: The shopping list here is built around one person: their favorite cheese, a second one you know they like, their favorite cured meat and their favorite crackers and jam. Getting those right says more than any expensive wedge would.
The rest is the board formula that makes anything look generous: good dark chocolate, strawberries and grapes for color, cashews or almonds for crunch and cornichons for a sharp, salty reset.

timeline.what: Think about what they actually love. Write it down.
Shop: good versions of familiar things, not unfamiliar expensive ones.
Take the cheese out of the fridge.
Light a candle. Put on something they like.

faq.q: What do you put on an apology charcuterie board?
faq.a: Their favorites first: the cheese, meat, crackers and jam they always pick. Then add dark chocolate, strawberries, grapes, nuts and cornichons so the board feels full and generous.

faq.q: What if I don't know their favorite cheese?
faq.a: Go with crowd-pleasers: a creamy brie and an aged cheddar or Gouda. Then remember what they eat first for next time.
About 3 oz of cheese and 3 oz of meat per person when the board is the snack, and less before a meal.
